⚠ Both ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set · auth may not work as expected
  · to use ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: Unset the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, or claude /logout then say "No" to the API key approval before
  login.
  · to use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: Unset the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable.

▎ Auto mode is now Claude Code's default permission mode.
▎ Auto mode lets Claude handle permission prompts automatically. Claude checks each tool call for risky actions and prompt injection before executing,
▎ runs the ones it assesses as lower-risk, and blocks the rest.
▎ https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes

❯ Call AskUserQuestion exactly once with 3 questions, copying text verbatim. Q1 header "Export", multiSelect false, question "Exporting readable
  WeChat history needs decrypting the local database with a key taken from the running WeChat, and there is no lighter way to do it. The safe version
  is doing that openly, on your own Mac and account, with every step logged. How do you want to proceed with the export of the full chat history?"
  options: label "GreenBubbles on my Mac, compiled and reviewed by us, with sudo and a one-time WeChat re-sign" desc "Recommended. MIT licensed, no
  telemetry, read-only, no plaintext DB left behind. Needs sudo, re-signing your WeChat.app (reverts on WeChat update), and one re-login (scan QR
  with your phone). Exports your local history to JSON and Markdown files."; label "yichen (gentler re-sign of a copy of WeChat)" desc "Signs a COPY
  of WeChat, so it does not touch your real app or need a re-login. But its licence is not open-source (personal use only) and it leaves a fully
  decrypted database on disk."; label "Screen-read new messages only" desc "No key extraction at all. Read-only on the server's secondary account,
  captures ongoing new messages in chosen groups, not full history. The most conservative, but not a real export."; label "Hold for now" desc "Do not
  read any WeChat database yet; keep thinking about it."
  Q2 header "Where", multiSelect false, question "这个导出结果准备放在哪里保存？请考虑隐私、备份以及之后是否需要让 Brain
  读取这些聊天记录来做摘要，另外还要考虑磁盘空间和加密需求，选一个最合适的位置。" options: label
  "放在本机加密磁盘镜像里，每次使用前手动挂载并输入密码" desc "最安全，但每次让 Brain 读取都要你在 Mac
  上手动挂载一次，不能全自动运行，也不方便手机上直接查看。"; label "放在家里 homelab 的加密卷，通过 Tailscale 访问" desc "可以自动化，Brain
  随时能读，但数据会离开 Mac，需要先配置好 homelab 上的加密和访问权限。"; label "放在普通文件夹" desc "最简单，没有加密。"
  Q3 header "Summary", multiSelect false, question "After the export, how should Brain summarize the groups?" options: label "Daily digest per group"
  desc "One short note per group per day."; label "Weekly digest only" desc "One note per week across all groups."; label "Only on demand" desc
  "Never summarize unless I ask."
  Reply with answers verbatim.

│ Exporting readable WeChat history needs decrypting the local database with a key taken from the running WeChat, and there is no lighter way to do
│ it. The safe version is doing that openly, on your own Mac and account, with every step logged. How do you want to proceed with the export of the
│ full chat history?

❯ 1. GreenBubbles on my Mac, compiled and reviewed by us, with sudo and a one-time WeChat re-sign
     Recommended. MIT licensed, no telemetry, read-only, no plaintext DB left behind. Needs sudo, re-signing your WeChat.app (reverts on WeChat
     update), and one re-login (scan QR with your phone). Exports your local history to JSON and Markdown files.
  2. yichen (gentler re-sign of a copy of WeChat)
     Signs a COPY of WeChat, so it does not touch your real app or need a re-login. But its licence is not open-source (personal use only) and it
     leaves a fully decrypted database on disk.
  3. Screen-read new messages only
     No key extraction at all. Read-only on the server's secondary account, captures ongoing new messages in chosen groups, not full history. The most
     conservative, but not a real export.
  4. Hold for now
     Do not read any WeChat database yet; keep thinking about it.
  5. Type something.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  6. Chat about this
